libraries.name: VideoToolbox
libraries.note: macOS frameworks fin-codecs will link (6B-1 Tasks 4–5, not built yet; objc2-video-toolbox, objc2-core-media, objc2-core-video): decode, pixel transfer (OS tone mapping) and H.264 encode. Linked as system frameworks, never loaded by name; part of the OS.

libraries.name: CoreMedia
libraries.note: macOS frameworks fin-codecs will link (6B-1 Tasks 4–5, not built yet; objc2-video-toolbox, objc2-core-media, objc2-core-video): decode, pixel transfer (OS tone mapping) and H.264 encode. Linked as system frameworks, never loaded by name; part of the OS.

libraries.name: CoreVideo
libraries.note: macOS frameworks fin-codecs will link (6B-1 Tasks 4–5, not built yet; objc2-video-toolbox, objc2-core-media, objc2-core-video): decode, pixel transfer (OS tone mapping) and H.264 encode. Linked as system frameworks, never loaded by name; part of the OS.

libraries.name: Media Foundation
libraries.note: Windows 11 Media Foundation that fin-codecs will use (6B-1 Tasks 6–7, not built yet; `windows` crate import libraries): MFStartup, MFTEnumEx and the stateful MFTs. Absent on N editions without the Media Feature Pack (CODEC_UNAVAILABLE with mediaFeaturePack guidance). Never loaded by name.

libraries.name: Microsoft MFTs
libraries.note: Microsoft's own decoder and encoder MFTs (vendor class os, plan Decision 3), including the Store extensions (HEVC Video Extensions, AV1 and VP9 extensions) the user installs. Activated through COM by MFTEnumEx, never loaded by name.

libraries.name: hardware MFTs
libraries.note: A GPU vendor's hardware decoder and encoder MFTs, installed with the driver (vendor class gpu, plan Decision 3). Activated through COM by MFTEnumEx, never loaded by name. Encoders: proxies only (owner decision 9, follow-up F3; fin_media::backend::encoder_allowed).

crates.note: fin-node's N-API bindings: on Windows (MSVC) napi-sys resolves the N-API symbols from the Node.js process that loaded the addon, falling back to an already-loaded or loadable node/libnode library (libloading). Node.js is the host, not something Finisher ships in fin-node.

fin-compositor's wgpu (spec §5.2): the D3D12 backend loads d3d12.dll and dxgi.dll, shader compilation uses FXC's d3dcompiler_47.dll (fin-compositor pins Dx12Compiler::Fxc, so dxcompiler.dll is never loaded), dcomp.dll only for window surfaces (never created), kernelbase.dll already loaded; the RenderDoc libraries are only opened when RenderDoc has already injected them (RTLD_NOLOAD, open_already_loaded); CoreGraphics only for Metal window surfaces. All are part of the OS or of a debugger the user runs.
wgpu's Vulkan backend loads the system Vulkan loader, installed with the GPU driver (or Mesa's lavapipe on GPU-less Linux, spec §5.2). Finisher bundles no Vulkan library.
